label: miso 48 stgas srmc
definition: MISO 48 ST_GAS_INTERMEDIATE SRMC-floor re-ground keeper candidate: the miso-47 keeper recipe re-solved byte-identical at HEAD with ONE offer-curve change - the generic ST_GAS_INTERMEDIATE committed band raised 0.85 -> 1.00x base_HR (backcast_config.py), closing the pjm-83 defect pattern from the L-7 SRMC-floor audit (docs/miso-caiso-srmc-floor-audit-2026-07.md SS2, G-21/#1302): an uncited generic sub-1.0 multiplier priced the five near-baseload MISO steam boilers (Harding Street, Ames, Nine Mile Point, Lewis Creek, Sabine) ~$3.3-5.2/MWh below the MISO cost-based-offer floor (Tariff Module C / Attachment L; IMM/Potomac SOM sanity). CC_REGULAR econ_low 0.95 untouched (the recognized CC flat-plateau CAMPD exception). Zero free parameters: a tariff-cited bound replaces a residual-lineage value; LOO degenerates to per-year direction checks, consistent all three years. Structure fix promoted on correctness (rules 1/11/14): 2023 ST_GAS crosses the C1 band edge (-7.56 -> -8.16 TWh, C1 14/16 -> 13/16) because the sub-SRMC band was buying ~0.6 TWh/yr of masked G-25 commitment-posture energy (now correctly attributed); C3a mean LMP improves in ALL years (2023 -0.1%, 2024 -4.7%, 2025 -10.7%). Everything else in the miso-47 recipe unchanged.
market_story: CT_PEAKER: MISO commits simple-cycle peakers for local Resource Adequacy through the afternoon-evening net-load ramp (the duck-neck: cooling load climbs while solar collapses at sunset); the evening [15,21] net-load floor reproduces that committed evening SHAPE the energy-only LP decommits (D-1 diurnal r~0.99, forced 5-7.5% under the peaker budget). ST_GAS: legacy gas-steam boilers are held warm at physical min-stable (0.12) through the overnight [0,6] trough on extreme-temperature / high-net-load days to ramp for the NEXT peak rather than pay a multi-hour cold start (forced 0.7-1.2%). Both are commitment scaffolding, not volume levers - the residual CT/ST_GAS annual under-run is a separate merit-position model miss (disclosed), not what the floor buys.
